## 1. Koide Formula & Mass Matrix

**Query:** `all:Koide` (sorted by submission date, descending)

The Koide formula is central to the PF's mass-generation mechanism — it encodes a leptonic mass relation with near-exact precision (2/3 ratio) that the PF aims to derive from propagation constraints on a discrete substrate.

### Top Pick

**[2606.10060] New sum rules of the Koide type**
- **Authors:** Alejandro Rivero
- **Published:** 2026-06-08 | **Category:** physics.gen-ph
- **Abstract:** Reports a mass rule of Koide type with inverse shape, m_i = M^(d)(w_0 + w_i)^(-2), applying to the down-quark sector with precision comparable to the charged-lepton sum rule. For central mass values, Koide ratio reaches exactly 2/3 near 280 TeV under SM renormalisation-group running. Also reviews other rules of the direct kind involving quarks.
- **PF Relevance:** HIGH. Extends Koide-type relations to the quark sector with the same 2/3 ratio that appears in the PF's triplet structure. The RG running to 280 TeV is interesting — the PF predicts structured mass hierarchies that should be visible at specific energy scales. This paper provides experimental targets (down-quark mass ratios) the PF must reproduce.
- **Links:** [abs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10060) | [pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.10060)

### Also Notable

**[2606.12693] Self-Reconstructing Codazzi Defects, CP¹ Quantization, and the Minimal Standard-Model Carrier**
- **Authors:** Piotr Ogonowski
- **Published:** 2026-06-10 (v2) | **Category:** physics.gen-ph
- **Abstract:** Formulates a filtered local reconstruction scheme for codimension-three Codazzi defects in 4D Lorentzian branches. The closure defect of the self-reconstruction loop is organized as a lexicographic residual fixing the projective link, Gauss-local charges, Toeplitz support, determinant carrier, finite shadow, torsor response, and Schur completion. Faithful reconstruction yields classification into V₁ and V₂ non-scalar types, and the resulting structure can accommodate SM gauge group and fermion content.
- **PF Relevance:** MEDIUM. Codazzi defects as a geometric origin for particle species — structurally reminiscent of the PF's approach to generating gauge groups from topological constraints. The "self-reconstructing" loop closure is analogous to the PF's propagation cycle. Worth watching for convergence with PF's discrete substrate model.
- **Links:** [abs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12693) | [pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.12693)

### Background

**[2606.08839] Time Evolution of Heat Conduction in a Generalized Model of Brownian Motion**
- **Authors:** T. Koide, F. Nicacio
- **Published:** 2026-06-07 | **Categories:** cond-mat.stat-mech, nucl-th, quant-ph
- **Abstract:** Investigates heat conduction in harmonic oscillators with generalized Brownian motion including noise and dissipation in both momentum and position equations, motivated by consistency with the GKSL equation. ## 2. Fisher Information & Particle Physics

**Query:** `abs:"Fisher information" AND cat:quant-ph` (sorted by submission date, descending)

Fisher information is the PF's bridge between geometry and physics — it provides the metric structure on the space of states that the PF identifies as the source of mass, force, and propagation dynamics.

### Top Pick

**[2607.07562] Relativistic Quantum Thermometry in AdS Spacetime via Non-Markovian Temperature Sensing**
- **Authors:** Anass Hminat, Abdallah Slaoui, Rachid Ahl Laamara
- **Published:** 2026-07-08 | **Category:** quant-ph
- **Abstract:** Characterizes temperature estimation accuracy in AdS spacetime using Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) and quantum signal-to-noise ratio. Introduces an ancillary Unruh-DeWitt detector between sensor and thermal bath, enhancing thermometric sensitivity by channeling temperature-dependent information into the probe qubit's coherence. Examines how detector acceleration in AdS affects QFI.
- **PF Relevance:** HIGH. Direct application of QFI as the fundamental precision metric in curved spacetime — this is precisely the PF's claim that the Fisher metric is the physical metric. The AdS setting provides a tractable model where the PF's Fisher-geometry-as-gravity hypothesis could be tested: if Fisher information determines physical geometry, then QFI bounds in AdS should match geodesic structure.
- **Links:** [abs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07562) | [pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.07562)

### Also Notable

**[2607.07434] Spectral-width limit on non-Hermitian quantum metrology**
- **Authors:** Jiaxin Liu, Zuoxian Wang, Danyue Ma
- **Published:** 2026-07-08 | **Category:** quant-ph
- **Abstract:** Proves that exponential amplification of QFI at exceptional points and via the skin effect does NOT represent genuine measurement information. For any open sensor with coherent parameter imprinting, the QFI is capped by the spectral width of the sensor's effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, independent of non-reciprocity or gain. Resolves the long-standing debate about whether non-Hermitian enhancements are real.
- **PF Relevance:** MEDIUM-HIGH. This is a crucial negative result for the PF — it establishes bounds on when Fisher information inflation is "fake" (non-reciprocal enhancement) vs. real (spectral width). The PF's claim that Fisher information IS the physical metric requires distinguishing genuine information from artifacts. This paper provides the mathematical criterion: spectral width is the ceiling.
- **Links:** [abs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07434) | [pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.07434)

**[2607.07031] Bayesian Gill-Massar Bound: An Attainable Lower Bound for Qubit Parameter Estimation**
- **Authors:** Ke-Han Zhao, Koichi Yamagata, Jun Suzuki
- **Published:** 2026-07-08 | **Category:** quant-ph
- **Abstract:** Studies lower bounds for Bayesian parameter estimation in qubit systems, deriving an attainable Gill-Massar bound that connects frequentist and Bayesian estimation frameworks for quantum systems.
- **PF Relevance:** MEDIUM. The Gill-Massar bound bridges the gap between frequentist (Fisher) and Bayesian (posterior) perspectives on quantum estimation. The PF uses a frequentist Fisher metric as its geometric foundation, but full consciousness physics may require the Bayesian generalization. This paper provides the formal connection.
- **Links:** [abs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07031) | [pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.07031)

## 3. Coherence in Quantum Field Theory

**Query:** `abs:coherence AND cat:quant-ph AND all:field theory` (sorted by submission date, descending)

Coherence is the PF's organizing principle — propagation creates coherent structures (particles, forces, spacetime) from an underlying substrate. Understanding coherence in QFT is understanding the PF's core mechanism.

### Top Pick

**[2607.08827] Exact Lindbladian Dynamics from Conformal Embeddings and Topological Defects in CFT**
- **Authors:** Chen Bai
- **Published:** 2026-07-09 | **Categories:** cond-mat.stat-mech, cond-mat.str-el, hep-th, quant-ph
- **Abstract:** Identifies intrinsic conformal structures that restore exact solvability in (1+1)D CFTs for open quantum systems. For N Majorana fermions with linear mode jumps, the adjoint Lindbladian is triangular on reduced even Majorana monomials, yielding recursive exact Heisenberg evolution. In WZW models admitting conformal Majorana embeddings, this hierarchy gives exact dynamics of affine-current products. Also reveals topological defects as sources of non-unitary evolution.
- **PF Relevance:** HIGH. This is a direct hit for the PF program. Exact solvability in open quantum CFTs via conformal embeddings is the kind of mathematical structure the PF needs to make its coherence claims rigorous. The Majorana fermion setting connects to the PF's interest in fermionic propagation modes. Topological defects as sources of non-unitary evolution — this is precisely the PF's claim about how propagation through a discrete substrate generates apparent non-unitarity (decoherence) from underlying unitary dynamics.
- **Links:** [abs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.08827) | [pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.08827)

### Also Notable

**[2607.09373] Deterministic Generation of Linear Photonic Cluster States with Semiconductor Quantum Dots**
- **Authors:** Nikolas Köcher, Stefan Schumacher
- **Published:** 2026-07-10 | **Category:** quant-ph
- **Abstract:** Theoretically compares four schemes for generating linear cluster states using semiconductor quantum dots, covering polarization and time-bin encoding across a range of cavity environments and spin coherence times. Studies how spin coherence limits fidelity.
- **PF Relevance:** MEDIUM. The systematic study of coherence as a limiting resource for quantum state generation is relevant to the PF's claim that coherence is the fundamental currency of physics. The spin coherence time as a bottleneck mirrors the PF's interest in propagation-distance-to-decoherence relationships.

**[2607.09162] Quaternary-Squeeze Quantum Identity Authentication**
- **Authors:** Zhipeng Chen, Haolun Tang, Xiao-Qi Xiao, Li-Hua Gong
- **Published:** 2026-07-10 | **Category:** quant-ph
- **Abstract:** Proposes QIA protocol using quadrature squeezed coherent states, exploiting quantum noise reduction to thwart eavesdropping via Heisenberg-limited uncertainty constraints. Uses fidelity parameters for decoy states to detect spoofing.
- **PF Relevance:** LOW-MEDIUM. Squeezed coherent states are a concrete realization of the PF's interest in minimum-uncertainty propagation modes. The protocol's reliance on coherence as a security resource is conceptually aligned with the PF's treatment of coherence as fundamental.
- **Links:** [abs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09162) | [pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.09162)

## 4. Quark Confinement & Discrete Symmetry

**Query:** `all:quark+confinement AND cat:hep-th` (sorted by submission date, descending)

The PF treats confinement not as a QCD-specific phenomenon but as a universal consequence of propagation constraints on a discrete substrate. Non-Abelian flux tubes and topological confinement mechanisms are direct analogs of the PF's propagation-boundary dynamics.

### Top Pick

**[2607.09485] Unified description of color-electric and color-magnetic strings in hybrid vacua of N=2 SQCD**
- **Authors:** E. Ievlev, D. Vasilev, A. Yung
- **Published:** 2026-07-10 | **Category:** hep-th
- **Abstract:** Studies non-Abelian strings in r-vacua of 4D N=2 SQCD with U(N) gauge group where both scalar quarks AND monopoles condense. This leads to flux tubes carrying both color-electric and color-magnetic fluxes, confining quarks AND monopoles simultaneously. Presents unified 2D effective worldsheet theory for these hybrid strings.
- **PF Relevance:** HIGH. Dual confinement (electric + magnetic) via a unified flux tube is structurally analogous to the PF's claim that propagation constraints generate both "matter" (electric) and "force" (magnetic) aspects from a single underlying mechanism. The 2D worldsheet theory is exactly the kind of effective description the PF predicts for propagation-boundary dynamics. If the PF is correct, confinement in N=2 SQCD should have a Fisher-information interpretation.
- **Links:** [abs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09485) | [pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.09485)

### Also Notable

**[2607.09531] Perusing confining pseudoreal theories: a story of emerging massless spin-1 bosons**
- **Authors:** Giacomo Cacciapaglia, Konstantinos Kollias
- **Published:** 2026-07-10 | **Categories:** hep-th, hep-lat, hep-ph
- **Abstract:** Comprehensive study of minimal asymptotically free pseudoreal theories with one or two Weyl fermion species in pseudoreal gauge representations. Identifies which theories flow to conformal dynamics vs. which confine with non-trivial condensate dynamics. Among confining theories, some exhibit emerging massless spin-1 bosons in the infrared.
- **PF Relevance:** MEDIUM-HIGH. The dichotomy between conformal and confining IR dynamics in pseudoreal theories is directly relevant to the PF's claim that propagation constraints determine whether a theory confines or not. The emergence of massless spin-1 bosons from confining dynamics is precisely the kind of "generation from constraint" the PF predicts. A natural test: does the PF's propagation framework predict which pseudoreal theories confine?
- **Links:** [abs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09531) | [pdf](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.09531)

**[2607.09354] Fully-beauty tensor tetraquark**
- **Authors:** S. S. Agaev, K. Azizi, H. Sundu
- **Published:** 2026-07-10 | **Categories:** hep-ph, hep-ex, hep-lat
- **Abstract:** Computes parameters of the fully-beauty tensor tetraquark T = bb(barb)(barb) using QCD sum rules. Mass prediction m = 18530 ± 86 MeV — stable against decays to η_b pairs and ΥΥ but unstable via bb-bar annihilation to light quarks.
